PullRequest.Title: test: quarantine confirmed cross-PR CI flakes
PullRequest.Body:
Written by Copilot.

## Summary

Quarantine four test scenarios only on their proven failing provider/platform variants. A September 24–26 Code OSS PR CI survey covered 557 workflow runs across 242 branches and 353 failed test-job logs, including failed attempts of eventually successful runs. Each quarantined scenario has same-run retry-pass evidence; the exact test execution was checked in successful logs.

| Tracking issue / triage owner | Quarantined variant | Observed recurrence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #338152 — @Giuspepe | Codex `retains context across consecutive turns`: Linux/macOS; `client-selected model is used for the turn`: Linux | 9 runs / 8 branches; 7 runs / 6 branches, respectively |
| #338153 — @Giuspepe | Codex `session changeset aggregates provider edits from default and peer chats`: Windows only | 6 runs / 6 branches |
| #338154 — @lszomoru | `Data Loss (insiders -> insiders) verifies that auto save triggers on shutdown`: remote Linux/Windows only | 12 runs / 11 branches |

Counts are distinct workflow runs, not duplicate logs or platform jobs. The two core Codex failures co-occur; a shared root cause is not yet established.

## Evidence

- Codex context/model on #338144: [failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36270407119/job/108483392832) → [both exact tests pass on the same head/base retry](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36270407119/job/108487986028).
- Same pair on an unrelated telemetry branch: [failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36240799731/job/108400793835) → [pass](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36240799731/job/108404630088).
- Windows Codex changeset: [failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36115631926/job/108008946124) → [exact test passes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36115631926/job/108015376556).
- Remote autosave: [failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36188982218/job/108249248234) → [exact test passes](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/36188982218/job/108260467143).

## Scope and re-enablement

- Preserve all test bodies, assertions, fixtures, existing capability gates, and unaffected provider/platform variants.
- Keep local/macOS autosave, other hot-exit tests, and stable-to-insiders smoke coverage enabled.
- Add issue-linked comments and active-gate documentation/reproduction instructions in Agent Host E2E `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`.
- Do not re-quarantine MCP/browser/marketplace failures already addressed by #337934, #337627, #338057, and #338032. Leave the newer two-branch connector-recording failure enabled pending more evidence.
- This is mitigation, not a root-cause fix. **Leave the three tracking issues open after merge** until their owners stabilize and re-enable the variants.

## Validation

- Passed 42 provider/platform/capability and remote-mode cases evaluating the actual quarantine expressions and smoke skip callback.
- Confirmed all three changed TypeScript files parse, and that removing only the intended gates restores their prior contents exactly.
- Targeted ESLint passed for all three changed TypeScript files.
- `git diff --check` and the normal commit hygiene hook passed.
- Full Electron/Windows/remote smoke suites were not run locally. CI results remain pending; no new test scenarios or runtime behavior are introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host core parity tests for context retention and client-selected model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At suite definition, the added provider/platform predicates perform only constant-time string/boolean checks. On affected Codex variants, Mocha registers skipped tests, so the test bodies do not create temporary workspaces, create sessions, or wait for model turns. On unaffected variants, the prior body and critical path are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a temporary workspace with mkdtempSync.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary directory per executed test; zero on the newly skipped Codex/platform combinations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both test bodies created their temporary workspace on every matching provider run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Was synchronous setup on the test critical path; the diff removes it for affected variants.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an Agent Host session and drive turns through TestProtocolClient.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The context test drives two sequential turns; the model-selection test drives one turn. The changed Codex/platform variants now execute zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same awaited calls ran on all eligible provider/platform combinations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each awaited session/turn had to complete before the test could progress; the diff removes these calls for affected variants.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exercise provider/model traffic while driving real-session turns (or its configured replay equivalent).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two turns for context retention and one for model selection per executed provider suite; zero for newly skipped variants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Affected Codex jobs previously executed these turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider responses were on the test critical path; the added gates suppress rather than add traffic.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Suite matrix cardinality: target/provider/platform combinations. Within each test the turn count is fixed (two and one respectively), with sequential awaits and no new burst concurrency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The test bodies await each session and turn serially. The added registration predicates schedule no asynchronous work and reduce aggregate concurrent CI load by skipping affected variants.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, cache lookup, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior is changed. Skipped variants perform neither cold nor warm session/model work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed predicates select test.skip before the bodies containing filesystem and protocol/model operations execute.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CI time and provider/replay latency vary, but the direction is strictly reduced work on affected jobs and unchanged work elsewhere.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes expensive work for targeted variants and adds only constant-time gating.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host session changeset aggregation parity test on Codex Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new boolean is computed during suite definition. On Codex Windows the test is registered skipped before workspace setup; elsewhere the existing git workspace, session/chat IPC, two provider turns, and polling remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and mutate a git-backed temporary workspace with two provider-created files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One workspace and two files per executed target/provider test; zero on newly skipped Codex Windows runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Codex Windows previously ran the same workspace setup and file edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Workspace creation and edits were required before assertions; the diff removes them on the quarantined variant.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a peer chat, subscribe to peer/session changeset channels, query changeset state, and list sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three initial client calls, two turn-driving flows, then serial polling with up to 100 attempts for changeset state and up to 100 attempts for listSessions per executed test; zero on newly skipped Codex Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The full IPC sequence and polling ran on every capable parity provider, including Codex Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All calls are awaited on the test critical path. The diff suppresses the entire sequence for Codex Windows rather than increasing calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the git-backed workspace and, for shell-strategy providers, execute file creation commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One git workspace and at most two provider file-creation commands per executed test; zero on the newly skipped variant.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The operations were already part of the test body and ran on eligible Codex Windows jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations precede aggregation assertions; the added gate removes them for Codex Windows.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One parity test per target/provider configuration; fixed two-chat cardinality. Retry polling is serial and bounded at 100 attempts per assertion, not multiplied by the new gate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two provider turns and both retry loops are sequentially awaited. No new Promise fan-out or aggregate concurrency is introduced; one platform/provider case is removed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Skipping occurs before workspace/session creation, so there are no cold or warm cache accesses on the quarantined variant.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added predicate directly changes test registration to test.skip before all expensive body operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual git, provider, and polling durations vary, but the diff can only reduce them on Codex Windows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only behavioral performance effect is reduced CI work on Codex Windows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote smoke test for auto-save during shutdown on Linux and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added in-test condition runs before testHotExit is called. On remote Linux/Windows, this.skip exits before createApp, process startup, editor automation, restart, and shutdown. Local runs, macOS remote runs, and other data-loss tests retain the old path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and start the VS Code application, restart it, and stop it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one start, one restart, and one stop for this test per remote Linux/Windows smoke job; now zero. Other variants are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote Linux/Windows jobs executed the full two-startup hot-exit test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Application lifecycle operations dominate and are awaited serially; the new skip occurs before application creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Configure auto-save, edit readme.md and an untitled file, persist state across restart, and read contents back.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed pair of edited documents and associated profile/log/crash filesystem activity per executed test; zero on newly skipped variants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same document and persistence operations ran on remote Linux/Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The operations are all after the new skip and were on the test critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Drive the application through the remote smoke-test connection when defaultOptions.remote is set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One remote test session with serial automation commands per affected job before the diff; none after the skip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The auto-save shutdown scenario ran over the configured remote connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote automation and restart had to complete for test progress; the new condition prevents the session from starting for targeted jobs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One test per smoke job and platform/remote variant, with a fixed number of application lifecycles and editor operations. The new condition does not scale with workspace size or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations within the test are sequentially awaited. The skip reduces process and remote-session concurrency in the overall CI matrix rather than creating a burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. The skip occurs before Application creation, so neither cold startup nor any warmed application state is consumed on targeted jobs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: this.skip executes before testHotExit, and all process/filesystem/remote operations are inside testHotExit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact remote startup and restart time varies by CI worker, but all such work is removed rather than added for the targeted variants.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change reduces startup, I/O, and remote automation work on the quarantined variants and leaves other paths unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. The PR adds documentation and narrowly scoped test skips; every transitive expensive boundary is either unchanged on unaffected variants or eliminated on affected variants. No actionable performance regression or qualifying shipped-regression fix was found.
